arxiv-1912-06472.title: Dimension of Reservoir Computers
arxiv-1912-06472.creator: T. L. Carroll
arxiv-1912-06472.description: Abstract A reservoir computer is a complex dynamical system, often created by coupling nonlinear nodes in a network. The nodes are all driven by a common driving signal. In this work, three dimension estimation methods, false nearest neighbor, covariance and Kaplan-Yorke dimensions, are used to estimate the dimension of the reservoir dynamical system.

arxiv-2010-13429.title: Propagating bands of plastic deformation in a metal alloy as critical avalanches
arxiv-2010-13429.creator: Tero Mäkinen, Pasi Karppinen, Markus Ovaska, Lasse Laurson, Mikko J. Alava
arxiv-2010-13429.description: Abstract The plastic deformation of metal alloys localizes in the Portevin–Le Chatelier effect in bands of different types, including propagating, or type ‘A’ bands, usually characterised by their width and a typical propagation velocity. This plastic instability arises from collective dynamics of dislocations interacting with mobile solute atoms but the resulting sensitivity to the strain-rate lacks fundamental understanding.

arxiv-2101-02983.title: Asymptotically optimal inference in sparse sequence models with a simple data-dependent measure This work is partially supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation, DMS–1811802.
arxiv-2101-02983.creator: Ryan Martin
arxiv-2101-02983.description: Abstract For high-dimensional inference problems, statisticians have a number of competing interests. On the one hand, procedures should provide accurate estimation, reliable structure learning, and valid uncertainty quantification. On the other hand, procedures should be computationally efficient and able to scale to very high dimensions.

arxiv-2205-06254.title: Learned Vertex Descent: A New Direction for 3D Human Model Fitting
arxiv-2205-06254.creator: Enric Corona 1, Gerard Pons-Moll 2,3, Guillem Alenyà 1, Francesc Moreno-Noguer 1
arxiv-2205-06254.description: Abstract We propose a novel optimization-based paradigm for 3D human model fitting on images and scans. In contrast to existing approaches that directly regress the parameters of a low-dimensional statistical body model ( e.g. SMPL) from input images, we train an ensemble of per vertex neural fields network.

arxiv-2301-03322.title: Simplifying Open-Set Video Domain Adaptation with Contrastive Learning Journal: Computer Vision and Image Understanding
arxiv-2301-03322.creator: Giacomo Zara, Victor Guilherme Turrisi da Costa, Subhankar Roy, Paolo Rota, Elisa Ricci
arxiv-2301-03322.description: Abstract In an effort to reduce annotation costs in action recognition, unsupervised video domain adaptation methods have been proposed that aim to adapt a predictive model from a labelled dataset (i.e., source domain) to an unlabelled dataset (i.e., target domain).

arxiv-2305-06123.title: Let It TEE: Asynchronous Byzantine Atomic Broadcast with n ≥ 2 ​ f + 1 n\geq 2f+1
arxiv-2305-06123.creator: Marc Leinweber, Hannes Hartenstein
arxiv-2305-06123.description: Abstract Asynchronous Byzantine Atomic Broadcast (ABAB) promises simplicity in implementation as well as increased performance and robustness in comparison to partially synchronous approaches. We adapt the recently proposed DAG-Rider approach to achieve ABAB with n ≥ 2 ​ f + 1 n\geq 2f+1 processes, of which f f are faulty, with only a constant increase in message size.

arxiv-2308-11175.description: Abstract . The goal of sequential recommendation (SR) is to predict a user’s potential interested items based on her/his historical interaction sequences. Most existing sequential recommenders are developed based on ID features, which, despite their widespread use, often underperform with sparse IDs and struggle with the cold-start problem.

arxiv-2410-20801.title: History-Matching of Imbibition Flow in Multiscale Fractured Porous Media Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs)
arxiv-2410-20801.creator: Jassem Abbasi, Ben Moseley, Takeshi Kurotori, Ameya D. Jagtap, Anthony R. Kovscek, Aksel Hiorth, Pål Østebø Andersen
arxiv-2410-20801.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jassem Abbasi, Ben Moseley, Takeshi Kurotori, Ameya D. Jagtap, Anthony R. Kovscek, Aksel Hiorth, Pål Østebø Andersen. In this work, we propose a workflow based on physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to model multiphase fluid flow in fractured porous media.

arxiv-2503-10542.title: Language Models, Graph Searching, and Supervision Adulteration: When More Supervision is Less and How to Make More More
arxiv-2503-10542.creator: Arvid Frydenlund
arxiv-2503-10542.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arvid Frydenlund. This work concerns the path-star task, a minimal example of searching over a graph. The graph, G G , is star-shaped with D D arms radiating from a start node, s s . A language model (LM) is given G G , s s , and a target node t t , which ends one of the arms and is tasked with generating the arm containing t t .

arxiv-2504-01666.title: CLIP-SLA: Parameter-Efficient CLIP Adaptation for Continuous Sign Language Recognition
arxiv-2504-01666.creator: Sarah Alyami Hamzah Luqman Information and Computer Science Department, King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals Computing Department, Imam Abdulrahman Bin Faisal University SDAIA–KFUPM Joint Research Center for Artificial Intelligence snalyami@iau.edu.sa hluqman@kfupm.edu.sa
arxiv-2504-01666.description: Abstract Continuous sign language recognition (CSLR) focuses on interpreting and transcribing sequences of sign language gestures in videos. In this work, we propose CLIP sign language adaptation (CLIP-SLA), a novel CSLR framework that leverages the powerful pre-trained visual encoder from the CLIP model to sign language tasks through parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT).

arxiv-2507-11817.title: Spectral extremal problems for non-bipartite graphs without odd cycles
arxiv-2507-11817.creator: Lantao Zou,Lihua Feng, Yongtao Li[3mm] School of Mathematics and Statistics, HNP-LAMACentral South University, Changsha, Hunan, 410083, China
arxiv-2507-11817.description: Abstract A well-known result of Mantel asserts that every n n -vertex triangle-free graph G G has at most ⌊ n 2 / 4 ⌋ \lfloor n^{2}/4\rfloor edges. Moreover, Erdős proved that if G G is further non-bipartite, then e ⁡ ( G ) ≤ ⌊ ( n − 1 ) 2 / 4 ⌋ + 1 e(G)\leq\lfloor{(n-1)^{2}}/{4}\rfloor+1 .

arxiv-2511-10675.title: Learn to Select: Exploring Label Distribution Divergence for In-Context Demonstration Selection in Text Classification
arxiv-2511-10675.creator: Ye Jiang, Taihang Wang, Youzheng Liu, Yimin Wang, Yuhan Xia, Yunfei Long
arxiv-2511-10675.description: Abstract In-context learning (ICL) for text classification, which uses a few input-label demonstrations to describe a task, has demonstrated impressive performance on large language models (LLMs). However, the selection of in-context demonstrations plays a crucial role and can significantly affect LLMs’ performance.

arxiv-2511-21774.title: Quantum Optimality in the Odd-Cycle game: the topological odd-blocker, marked connected components of the giant, consistency of pearls, vanishing homotopy
arxiv-2511-21774.creator: Pete Rigas
arxiv-2511-21774.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pete Rigas. We characterize optimality of Quantum strategies for the Odd-Cycle game. Separate from other game-theoretic settings, parallel repetition for the Odd-Cycle game is related to the foam problem, which can be formulated through a minimization of the surface area. In comparison to previous works on minimizing the surface area, we quantify how properties of the marked giant connected component can be related to the maximum winning probability using Quantum strategies.

arxiv-2602-08934.title: StealthRL: Reinforcement Learning Paraphrase Attacks for Multi-Detector Evasion of AI-Text Detectors
arxiv-2602-08934.creator: Suraj Ranganath, Atharv Ramesh
arxiv-2602-08934.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Suraj Ranganath, Atharv Ramesh. AI-text detectors face a critical robustness challenge: adversarial paraphrasing attacks that preserve semantics while evading detection. We introduce StealthRL , a reinforcement learning framework that stress-tests detector robustness under realistic adversarial conditions. StealthRL trains a paraphrase policy against a multi-detector ensemble using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with LoRA adapters on Qwen3-4B, optimizing a composite reward that balances detector evasion with semantic preservation.

pmc-11436893.title: Detection of breast cancer in digital breast tomosynthesis with vision transformers
pmc-11436893.creator: Idan Kassis, Dror Lederman, Gal Ben-Arie, Maia Giladi Rosenthal, Ilan Shelef, Yaniv Zigel
pmc-11436893.description: Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) has revolutionized more traditional breast imaging through its three-dimensional (3D) visualization capability that significantly enhances lesion discernibility, reduces tissue overlap, and improves diagnostic precision as compared to conventional two-dimensional (2D) mammography. In this study, we propose an advanced Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) system that harnesses the power of vision transformers to augment DBT’s diagnostic efficiency.

pmc-11649916.title: A microgripper based on electrothermal Al–SiO2 bimorphs
pmc-11649916.creator: Hengzhang Yang, Yao Lu, Yingtao Ding, Ziyue Zhang, Anrun Ren, Haopu Wang, Xiaoyi Wang, Jiafang Li, Shuailong Zhang, Huikai Xie
pmc-11649916.description: Microgrippers are essential for assembly and manipulation at the micro- and nano-scales, facilitating important applications in microelectronics, MEMS, and biomedical engineering. To guarantee the safe handling of delicate materials and micro-objects, a microgripper needs to be designed to operate with exceptional precision, rapid response, user-friendly operation, strong reliability, and low power consumption.

pmc-12504070.title: Givenness hierarchy theoretic sequencing of robot task instructions
pmc-12504070.creator: Zhao Han, Daniel Hammer, Kevin Spevak, Mark Higger, Aaron Fanganello, Neil T. Dantam, Tom Williams
pmc-12504070.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionWhen collaborative robots teach human teammates new tasks, they must carefully determine the order to explain different parts of the task. In robotics, this problem is especially challenging, due to the situated and dynamic nature of robot task instruction.MethodIn this work, we consider how robots can leverage the Givenness Hierarchy to “think ahead” about the objects they must refer to so that they can sequence object references to form a coherent, easy-to-follow series of instructions.Results and discussionOur experimental results (n = 82)

pmc-12653826.title: Nicotinamide and Pyruvate as Potential Therapeutic Interventions for Metabolic Dysfunction in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma—A Narrative Review
pmc-12653826.creator: Nathan Schanzer, Alon Harris, Kunal Kanwar, Rick Mortensen, Alice Verticchio Vercellin, Francesco Oddone, Carmela Carnevale, Keren Wood, Brent Siesky, Alessio Martucci
pmc-12653826.description: Mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress have been suggested as potential contributors to the initiation and progression of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Nicotinamide and pyruvate are important in the human body for maintaining metabolic function and preserving cytoskeletal structures. Both substances show an age-dependent decline in humans which may contribute to metabolic dysfunction and POAG vulnerability.

pmc-12682028.creator: Stephan Schorn, Helmut Friess, Ihsan Ekin Demir
pmc-12682028.description: nts, Germany's record of universal, high-quality surgical care is at risk. pmc-12744807.title: Evaluating the Comparative Effectiveness of Sodium-Glucose Transporter 2 Inhibitors (SGLT-2i) on Liver Enzymes in Patients With Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease: A Comprehensive Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

pmc-12744807.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to conduct the first network meta-analysis (NMA) comparing the effectiveness of sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors—dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ipragliflozin—in improving liver-related and metabolic outcomes in patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), utilizing a robust Bayesian NMA framework.

pmc-12865946.title: Association of high-fat diet with bone mineral density in older U.S. adults: a cross-sectional study of NHANES 2017–2018
pmc-12865946.creator: Na Li, Qing He, Yuan Cheng, Tao Jin
pmc-12865946.description: BackgroundEvidence on the relationship between dietary fat intake and bone mineral density (BMD) remains inconsistent, particularly regarding sex- and site-specific differences in femoral bone health among older adults.MethodsThis cross-sectional study analyzed data from the 2017–2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) to explore associations between dietary fat intake and femoral BMD in U.S. adults aged ≥ 50 years.

pmc-13198786.title: Collet–Sicard syndrome resulting from a Skull Base Paraganglioma: a case report
pmc-13198786.creator: Abhishek Man Shrestha, Subodh Bashyal, Suman Bhattarai, Lekhjung Thapa
pmc-13198786.description: Collet–Sicard syndrome is a rare neurological condition resulting from lesions at the jugular foramen and hypoglossal canal, leading to combined palsy of cranial nerves IX, X, XI, and XII. Neoplastic causes are most commonly involved, while benign tumors such as paragangliomas are infrequent etiologies. We report a 58-year-old woman who presented with progressive dysphagia and unilateral lower cranial nerve dysfunction.

pmc-13269192.title: The Impact and Reliability of Tissue Segmentation on In Vivo Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy Metabolite Quantification
pmc-13269192.creator: Jessica Archibald, Kay Chioma Igwe, Antonia Kaiser, Karl Landheer, Jaimie Lee, John L K Kramer, Aaron T Gudmundson, Helge J Zöllner, Georg Oeltzschner, Candace C Fleischer, Niklaus Zölch, Jamie Near, Mark Mikkelsen
pmc-13269192.description: PurposeQuantification of metabolite concentrations using MRS requires tissue‐dependent signal corrections. Accurate estimation of voxel tissue composition is therefore essential. Commonly used brain tissue segmentation tools differ in their algorithms and implementation, potentially introducing variability in MRS‐derived concentration estimates. This study investigates the impact and reliability of tissue segmentation on metabolite quantification.
